findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. The Moving branch sets the row's state but never copies `next.step` into `row.next`. Normal working and reviewing items have steps such as “wait for the review, then forge close <item>” (`src/forge/nextstep.py:52-53`), yet the Board tab shows only their stage and elapsed time. This leaves the Done-when requirement that each item show its next step unmet.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The mounted Board-tab fixture gives its Moving row no `next.step`, and the assertion checks only its running state. The command-level Moving fixture likewise omits `next.step` (`tests/test_fix_pane_grouped_board.py:96`). These tests pass while the Board tab drops a real working or reviewing item's next step.
findings.title: Not done: Test Moving rows' next steps through the Board tab

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Gate. The recorded allowance calls this a grouped-pane fix, but this line adds `step` to public `forge next --json`, `src/forge/board.py:505` adds `needs_person` to public `forge board --json`, and `src/forge/mod/hooks/register.ts:10` changes refresh timing. The diff therefore includes machine-interface and refresh-contract changes, which fail the allowance rule requiring one kind of problem without an interface change.
findings.title: Recorded allowance covers multiple problems and interface changes
